- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% above recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33) and price is falling, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Model consistently underestimates in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.00–0.50); apply 1–2% upward bias.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or declining; forecast should align with 10–14-day moving average, not 30-day.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.50 → -0.33 → +0.50), model overreacts; dampen forecast volatility by 20–30% in next 5 days.
